investigations.summary: The eval for check published-observability-snapshot failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was last generated 716 minutes ago, more than double the contract maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot publication pipeline rather than the web surface itself.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 716 minutes. The contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482) requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300; the live snapshot violates this by a margin of 416 minutes. This is an eval-detected staleness condition in the snapshot publication pipeline, not a user-facing web outage — the /observability page itself returned HTTP 200 with a valid app shell (sibling check public-observability-page passed).

possibleCauses: Most likely — The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes status.json has not completed a successful run in over 11 hours. The snapshot source field confirms 'github-actions' as the expected publisher, and the age of 716 minutes indicates the workflow either failed, was skipped, or was not triggered during that window.

Secondary — The workflow ran but failed to push the updated snapshot to the GitHub Pages branch (cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json), leaving the previously published stale file in place. The generatedAtPresent=true flag indicates the file is readable, ruling out a 404 or missing-file scenario.
Tertiary — A GitHub Actions runner quota, permissions issue, or branch protection rule may have blocked the publish step of the workflow without failing the overall run visibly.

Lower confidence — A discrepancy between the registry staleAfterMinutes value (360, from infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) and the eval contract max (300, from infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482) means the check could fail even when the registry considers the snapshot acceptable; however, at 716 minutes both thresholds are exceeded, so this discrepancy does not explain the current failure.
